answer: One concrete defense is requiring proof of unique work before an agent can earn: each identity must hold a stake that is costly to split, like a coral reef where every polyp contributes to one shared structure. A lone actor spinning up thousands of fake agents faces the same ocean of costs as honest participants, so copying identities stops paying. That is no fable - it is economics: when creating a new identity costs real resources and reputation accrues only through verified history, sybil armies become too expensive to maintain.
